issues.legal_issue: Rental income from property let by a company is included in its business profits for excess profits tax where the letting is connected with the company’s business.
material_facts: The assessee was a banking company that constructed a six-storeyed building, occupied part of it for its offices, and let the remainder to tenants.
The portion let to tenants was substantially larger than the portion used by the bank, and the Tribunal found that the building had been constructed partly to earn rent.
The company’s memorandum authorised acquiring and managing property and realising rents as activities connected with its business.
The rent at issue was assessed to excess profits tax, but the High Court held that it was not business income because the company did not mainly hold investments or property.
issues.conclusion: The majority held that the rental income was part of the company’s business profits and was liable to be included in computing excess profits tax; the appeal was allowed and the High Court’s decision was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(5), 2(19), 4 and 5 of the Excess Profits Tax Act, 1940, read with rule 4(4) of Schedule I, the definition of business is not confined to the first proviso’s category of companies whose functions consist wholly or mainly in holding investments or property. The main definition may independently cover activities connected with a company’s business, and rule 4(4) includes income from property where the business consists wholly or partly in letting property on hire. The memorandum of association may indicate the company’s business objects, and business can include a continuing or quiescent activity. The majority relied on Commissioners of Inland Revenue v. Desoutter Bros. Ltd. on the independent reach of the main definition; Commissioners of Inland Revenue v. The South Behar Railway Co. Ltd. and Commissioners of Inland Revenue v. The Korean Syndicate Ltd. on quiescent business activity; Punjab Co-operative Bank Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax and Sardar Indra Singh and Sons Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax on business income connected with normal business operations; and Inland Revenue Commissioners v. Gittus on giving effect to clear Schedule language. The Tyre Investment Trust case was also discussed in rejecting the argument that the first proviso would be redundant.

rule.if: excess_profits_tax_business_income_case and company_business_authorizes_property_management and property_held_or_used_in_business and property_let_for_rent

predicates.excess_profits_tax_business_income_case: The proceeding concerns whether income is included in business profits for excess profits tax.
predicates.company_business_authorizes_property_man: The company’s governing business objects include acquiring or managing property or realising rent from it.
predicates.property_held_or_used_in_business: The company holds or uses the property as part of activities connected with its business.
predicates.property_let_for_rent: The company lets all or part of the property to tenants and receives rent.
predicates.rental_income_included_in_business_profi: The rental income is included in the company’s business profits.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns excess profits tax, the company’s business objects include property management, the property is connected with its business, and it is let for rent, the rental income is included in business profits.
